description_full: Vontier Corporation provides mobility ecosystem solutions worldwide. It operates through three segments: Mobility Technologies, Repair Solutions, and Environmental and Fueling Solutions. The Mobility Technologies segment provides digitally enabled equipment and operating software solutions for mobility ecosystem, such as convenience retail operating platform, point-of-sale and payment solutions, remote diagnostics and site-management tools, workflow automation solutions, data analytics, operating software platform for electric vehicle charging networks, integrated solutions for alternative fuel dispensing, and IoT-based fleet telematics. Its Repair Solutions segment manufactures and distributes aftermarket vehicle repair tools, toolboxes, automotive diagnostic equipment and software through mobile franchise network. The Environmental and Fueling Solutions segment offers environmental monitoring and leak detection systems, forecourt controllers, vapor recovery equipment, and fuel dispenser systems for petroleum under the Gilbarco and Veeder-Root brands. The company markets its products and services to retail and commercial fueling, convenience store, and car wash operators; commercial vehicle repair businesses, fleet owners/operators and electric vehicle charging network operators, as well as direct sales personnel and independent distributors. It serves customers in North America, the Asia Pacific, Europe, and Latin America. Vontier Corporation was incorporated in 2019 and is headquartered in Raleigh, North Carolina.

financial_summary: Vontier Corporation is a mid-cap technology business with a $5.7B market cap on $3.1B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -1% over the past three years — essentially flat, and a business treading water is rarely a path to compounding.
Returns on capital run at 16% against a 8% cost of capital, a 7-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it, with gross margins sitting at 45%.

The business throws off $441M in free cash flow — roughly 14 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.26× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 2.6× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and interest coverage runs at 8.1×.

Management returns a meaningful 5.5% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.

sect: Its 18% operating margin runs 11pp above the Technology median (7%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It earns less of the sector's profit than its revenue share would suggest (0.78x).
Over five years it has been losing share of the sector profit pool (-11.2% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 530 companies in the universe; the top four hold 29% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares have drifted lower, down 13% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has rebounded 13% over the last three months.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 12% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 30% and a beta of 1.05, it moves roughly with the market, though its beta has shifted (1y 0.15 vs 5y 1.06), so read it loosely.
About $41.4M trades a day, enough to build a position.
In past sell-offs it fell 10% in the 2020 crash and 46% in the 2022 bear market.
val: The stock trades 27% below its DCF fair value of $57.66, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 33%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $43.09 to $79.25 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Technology peers: P/E 17.3 vs 26.7, EV/EBITDA 10.4 vs 16.4 and P/FCF 12.9 vs 25.4 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 11% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are mixed: an FCF yield of 7.7% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 7.6% (vs the 8% bar).
The 10 covering analysts target $40.85 on average, 3% below the price.
prof: ROIC of 16% clears the cost of capital of 8.4% by 7pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have been steady (CV 0.17).
It runs a 45% gross margin and converts 14% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 1.26x.
ROE of 33% is amplified by 3.5x balance-sheet leverage (DuPont), so ROIC is the cleaner read on the business.
It spends 5.7% of revenue on R&D and 1.0% on stock compensation.
hlth: Leverage is moderate at 2.6x net debt to EBITDA ($492.2M of cash against $2.1B of debt), above the 1.5x gate, with interest covered 8.1x.
Goodwill makes up 40% of assets, a soft asset exposed to impairment.
growth: Revenue has compounded at -1.2% over 3 years and 2.6% over 5 years, so growth is decelerating.
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
Free cash flow has compounded -7.6% a year over five years, short of the 5% durability bar.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 0.99, a backlog worth 14% of annual revenue and deferred revenue down 19%.
Capex roughly matches depreciation (1.4x, 2.3% of sales), a maintenance pace.
Its Rule of 40 score is 16, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.8%), and reported institutional holdings exceed 100% of shares (a sign of heavy share lending).
It returns 5.5% a year to shareholders (5.3% in buybacks and 0.2% in dividends).
The share count has shrunk 4.6% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
Short interest is elevated at 12.1% of the float, 9.3 days to cover.
people: With about 7,800 employees, each generates about $394K of revenue, in line with the Technology median, and productivity has risen 2.6% a year.
That works out to $57K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $3.4M (9x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores well (2/10, lower is better).
